raidSayLines.line: A person, maybe 30s, with sun-creased eyes: "Nothing grows here but dirt and tents. Past the treeline — that's where the green is. That's where the food is."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.

It followed you. The dog-shaped silence at the treeline is here.

⚔ A DOG-SHAPED SILENCE AT THE TREELINE! You're on your own.

💡 COUNTER LEARNED — a dog-shaped silence at the treeline: Wound the lead. Wound the lead and the pack breaks. Hit the FIRST wolf — the one that came in first — and the coordination dies. They fear fire, but breaking the lead is free.

a dog-shaped silence at the treeline is hurt — and it goes quiet and clever. It stops rushing. It starts CHOOSING. Watch the spacing.

🌙 The night shift is out: a dog-shaped silence at the treeline. They own the dark — the cast turns over after sunset, and every step is riskier. A lit fire is a beacon — light through canvas, smoke on the wind. Sealed and dark, you're just a smell in the night. Haven's walls end every argument.
